title: Medicine
note: Diseases come from past deeds and from causes such as unsuitable food and actions. Those from past deeds end only when the deeds are spent, so this chapter sets them aside and tells the medicine for the rest.

couplets.plain: Too much or too little, and the three the learned list, starting with wind, will cause disease.
couplets.pm: When food and activity go beyond or fall short of what suits your constitution, the three disorders the medical books count, starting with wind, trouble you. They class constitutions as wind, bile and phlegm. Food suits when taste, potency and amount fit. Activity suits when you stop work of mind, speech and body before it tires them.

couplets.plain: The body needs nothing called medicine if you eat only after making sure that what you ate has been digested.
couplets.pm: If you know clearly by the signs that what you ate before has been digested, and only then eat, your body needs no other medicine. The signs are lightness of body, clean belching, senses fit for their work, and strong hunger. “If you eat” shows how rare this is.

links.quote: The body needs nothing called medicine

couplets.plain: When your food has been digested, eat knowing the measure. That is how someone who has a body makes it last.
couplets.pm: When what you ate is digested, eat only as much as you know will digest. That is how a man who has escaped countless other bodies and won this rare human one carries it a long way. This body alone can reach this world, the next and release, and the longer it lasts the more of these it can gain.

links.quote: When your food has been digested, eat knowing the measure
links.reason: Gives someone unwell from eating a plain rule: eat in measure, and only after the last meal has gone.

couplets.plain: Know that your food is digested, get properly hungry, and take care to eat only what doesn’t disagree with you.
couplets.pm: Know that what you ate is digested, then grow very hungry, and when you eat, take care to choose food that doesn’t disagree. Food must not clash with your constitution, with the season or hour, or within itself, as honey and ghee in equal parts turn to poison. Eating as you please brings disease and death.

couplets.plain: Eat food that doesn’t disagree with you, and stop short, and your life will come to no harm.
couplets.pm: Eat food free of those three clashes, not in the amount your heart wants but in the amount that keeps disease away, and disease won’t bring suffering to your life. It is the soul that suffers, so he speaks of it. Even with food that doesn’t clash, less is better.

links.quote: stop short, and your life will come to no harm
links.reason: Eating sparingly of what agrees with you keeps your life free of harm.

couplets.plain: Joy stays with someone who knows to eat a little less. In the same way, disease stays with someone who gorges.
couplets.pm: As joy never leaves the man who knows that less is better and eats a little short of what he could, disease never leaves the man who swallows huge feeds. Joy means the three humours stay in place, so mind, speech and body are his own, and he gains the four aims, beginning with righteousness. The other is like an animal that feeds without measure and suffers by it.

links.quote: disease stays with someone who gorges
links.reason: Has joy stay with the light eater and disease with the glutton.

couplets.plain: Someone who eats without thought, more than the fire can take, will have diseases without measure.
couplets.pm: A man who doesn’t consider his constitution, the right food or the right time, and eats whatever he likes, whenever he likes, far beyond the fire in his belly, will find his diseases grow without limit.

links.quote: more than the fire can take
links.reason: Eating past what the body’s fire can take breeds disease without limit.

couplets.plain: Find the disease, find its cause, find the way to ease it, and act so that it works.
couplets.pm: A physician should settle from the signs what disease the patient has, then work out its cause, then find the way to cure it, and carry that out without error. The cause is the food and activity named above. The way covers giving medicine, letting blood, cutting, burning and the like. Without error means not straying from the practice of the old physicians.

links.quote: Find the disease, find its cause, find the way to ease it

couplets.plain: The one who has learned should weigh the patient, the disease and the time, and then act.
couplets.pm: A physician learned in medicine should, as his texts direct, weigh the patient, the disease and the time for his work, and act to fit them. The patient means constitution, age and strength to bear pain. The disease means whether it is curable, incurable or manageable, its stage and its force. Weigh these by the books and by keen judgement.

links.quote: weigh the patient, the disease and the time
links.reason: Tells the learned healer which three things to weigh before treating.

couplets.plain: The patient, the healer, the remedy and the attendant: medicine has these four parts.
couplets.pm: Medicine has four parts, each with four qualities. The sufferer needs wealth, obedience, clear report and endurance. The physician needs no fear, learning, experience and purity. The remedy needs broad use, potency, ease of getting and fit. The one who prepares it needs loving-kindness, purity, exactness and understanding. A cure needs them all, so all are called medicine.

links.reason: Places the healer as one of the four on whom recovery rests.
